{{nihongo|'''Takechino Miagata Shrine'''|高市御県神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kashihara, Nara|Q496319|qid=Q496319}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=unranked shrine}}. {{nihongo|'''Takechino Miagata Shrine'''|高市御県神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

==Enshrined deities==
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsu-hikone-no-Mikoto}} (あまつひこねのみこと) 
*{{ill|Takamimusubi|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi-no-Kami}} (たかみむすびのかみ)

== History ==
== Outline ==
The date of foundation is unknown, but in the {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} era it is recorded as "Takechi no Agata Shrine, two households of {{ill|Shinpo|Q1689534|qid=Q1689534}}" (''{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|Q11502312|qid=Q11502312}}''), suggesting it already existed before then. In the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' it is listed as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}, and along with Takechi, Katsuraki, Tōichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu, it was one of the "{{ill|The Six Prefectures of Wa|Q55521849|qid=Q55521849|lt=Six Miagata Shrines of Yamato Province}}" and received deep reverence from the {{ill|Imperial Court of Japan|Q30253177|qid=Q30253177|lt=imperial court}}. In the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, it was called "Takagata-no-miya" and "Jūsansha (sho) Daimyōjin."
